source.text:
name: clew-weather-demo
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:18.3
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: weather
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: weather
    volumes:
      - weather-data:/var/lib/postgresql
      - ./database/init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: [CMD-SHELL, pg_isready -U weather]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30
  kafka:
    image: apache/kafka:4.1.2
    environment:
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: 1
      KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: broker,controller
      KAFKA_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092
      KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: CONTROLLER
      KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: 1@kafka:9093
      KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: 1
      KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: 1
      KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: 'true'
    healthcheck:
      test: [CMD-SHELL, '/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --list']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 30
  kafka-init:
    image: apache/kafka:4.1.2
    entrypoint: ["/bin/bash", "-ec"]
    command:
      - |
        for topic in weather.place-requested weather.forecast-updated; do
          /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --create --if-not-exists --topic "$$topic" --partitions 1 --replication-factor 1
          /opt/kafka/bin/kafka-topics.sh --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --topic "$$topic"
        done
    depends_on:
      kafka: {condition: service_healthy}
  places:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: services/places/Dockerfile
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: Host=postgres;Database=places;Username=weather;Password=weather
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP: kafka:9092
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:8081:8080']
    depends_on:
      postgres: {condition: service_healthy}
      kafka-init: {condition: service_completed_successfully}
  forecasts:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: services/forecasts/Dockerfile
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/forecasts
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP: kafka:9092
      FORECAST_MODE: ${FORECAST_MODE:-fixture}
      MET_USER_AGENT: ${MET_USER_AGENT:-}
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:8082:8080']
    depends_on:
      postgres: {condition: service_healthy}
      kafka-init: {condition: service_completed_successfully}
  dashboard:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: services/dashboard/Dockerfile
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://weather:weather@postgres:5432/dashboard
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP: kafka:9092
      PLACES_URL: http://places:8080
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:8080:8080']
    depends_on:
      postgres: {condition: service_healthy}
      kafka-init: {condition: service_completed_successfully}
volumes:
  weather-data:

fragment.text: A caller enters Dashboard.requestRefresh with a place ID. Dashboard URL-encodes the ID in a bodyless POST /places/{id}/refresh with a 10-second timeout; the saved Dashboard-to-Places mapping is agent-proposed, so runtime routing is unverified. Places.Refresh calls Find; Find returns the first ID match from List. If no place is found, Refresh returns 404 PLACE_NOT_FOUND before enqueue. Otherwise it awaits Enqueue, which opens a connection, begins a transaction, inserts a request_outbox row with a new GUID and a place.requested v1 payload, then commits before Refresh returns 202 with status QUEUED. QUEUED marks the response, not forecast completion. Dashboard forwards upstream status and parsed JSON; a fetch or JSON-decoding exception becomes 503 PLACES_UNAVAILABLE, which does not show whether Places committed first. Open disposes and rethrows on connection-open failure; other exception-to-HTTP handling is outside these bodies. The saved process links separate Places publisher and Dashboard/Forecasts consumer views, but this path does not establish publication or delivery. These wrappers show no idempotency key or repeated-request deduplication.
